why: I compared each of the seven verifier checks with its expect line. Checks 1–4 only require the exact stdout plus a newline, and check 1 also requires exit 0, which is what the words say. Check 5 requires the JSON text with "\t" as the two-character escape. That matches the literal expected output and the issue's proof. Check 6 requires only that `npm test` exits 0 and that some test "runs bin/csv2json.js with the --tsv argument, gives it input that contains tab characters, and asserts on the output". It is judged on `npm test`, not `npm run test:cli`. Check 7 requires only that README.md mentions --tsv and shows an example that uses it, with the exact form given only as "for example". The stricter points (exact-string assertions, flag position, README saying "tab-separated", non-goal scope, test:cli) all sit under Advisory. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its expect line says.
